## Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Evidence reviewed
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames, 3,576s duration)
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export)
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.jpg` (screenshot of same alerts, not independently reviewed beyond the text export)

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | Sole local host generating all outbound suspicious traffic; DHCP-assigned at frame 1-4 |
| MAC | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==172.17.0.99` resolves to this MAC; same MAC appears as `dhcp.hw.mac_addr` for hostname `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT` |
| Hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (domain `bepositive.com`, NetBIOS/workgroup `BEPOSITIVE`) | DHCP option 12, NBNS registration (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>/<20>`), DNS dynamic update `SOA bepositive.com ... A 172.17.0.99` |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 172.17.0.99 and the DC (172.17.0.17) |

Local domain controller for reference: **172.17.0.17**, MAC `00:23:ae:50:ba:fd`, hostname `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com` (DHCP server, DNS server, LDAP/Kerberos authority — not the victim, this is the domain's DC).

### Malware family
**Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed**. The alert export contains:
```
ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2
172.17.0.99 -> 79.124.78.197, sport=49813 -> dport=80, count=48
```
This is corroborated behaviorally in the pcap: 172.17.0.99 repeatedly (~48 times over the ~1-hour capture) sends `POST /foots.php` to `79.124.78.197:80` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, a spoofed IE7/Windows-10 user agent, and a pipe-delimited body starting with a status code and a persistent bot GUID, e.g.:
```
101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
102|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654
```
The same session also performs a gate check-in:
- `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` → response `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`
- `POST /index.php` → 200 OK with a small (105-byte) non-ASCII/encrypted response body (encrypted config or module, not further decodable from ciphertext alone).

The C2 IP is contacted with no preceding DNS lookup (bare-IP `Host: 79.124.78.197` header), consistent with a hardcoded C2 IP typical of commodity stealer builds.

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — evidence: repeated `POST /foots.php` and `/index.php` HTTP flows from 172.17.0.99, matches ET Koi Stealer signature (tcp.stream 48, 51, 56, 63, 68, 71, 73, ... continuing every ~60-90s through end of capture)

**URLs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — primary stealer C2 checkin/exfil endpoint, ~48 POSTs observed
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — gate GET request, returns bot token
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — POST that receives an encrypted/binary response payload

**Bot identifiers (host-specific artifacts, useful for hunting)**
- Bot GUID: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`
- Sub ID: `qIOuKk7U`

**Domains**
- None — the C2 is contacted directly by IP with no DNS resolution in this capture.

**Files / hashes**
- No executable or malware binary was transferred over HTTP in this capture (beaconing is already active at t=155s from capture start, meaning initial infection predates or falls outside this recording). The `/foots.php` and `/index.php` bodies are raw data blobs/tokens, not named files, so no meaningful malware-sample SHA256 can be produced from this pcap. I am not fabricating a hash for a file that was not observed.

### Benign context (not IOCs)
- `bepositive.com` / `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19` — internal AD domain and DC, all Kerberos/LDAP/DHCP/DNS traffic to 172.17.0.17
- GPL NETBIOS/RPC "overflow" alerts (`SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP ... overflow`, `SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0`, `RPC kerberos principal name overflow`) between 172.17.0.99 and 172.17.0.17 — these are normal Windows domain authentication traffic (NTLMSSP/Kerberos/SMB), a well-known false-positive pattern for these legacy GPL signatures, not evidence of exploitation
- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `dns.msftncsi.com` — Windows NCSI connectivity checks (the "Terse Request .txt - Likely Hostile" / "Microsoft Connection Test" alerts are FPs on this benign NCSI check)
- Microsoft telemetry/services: `login.microsoftonline.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `odc.officeapps.live.com`, `ecs.office.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `*.msn.com`, `*.bing.com`
- `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org` — Windows CryptoAPI trust-list/cert revocation updates
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` — Adobe telemetry (`ProcessMAU.txt`)
- `sso.godaddy.com`, `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201, TLS-only, largest byte conversation at 719 kB) — no malicious signal tied to either; likely unrelated user browsing

### Incident summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** on the `bepositive.com` AD domain, is infected with **Koi Stealer** (ET Pro signature-confirmed). Throughout the capture the host beacons to its C2 at **79.124.78.197:80**, POSTing bot-tagged data blobs to `/foots.php` roughly every 60-90 seconds under bot GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`, and separately checks in via an `/index.php` gate that returns an encrypted payload. The infection vector (how the stealer arrived) is not observable in this capture, since C2 traffic is already active within the first three minutes of recording.
